sql:
select cls,
  floor(fish_date_doy/10)*10 as doy_bucket,
  count(*) n,
  sum(yt)/sum(anglers) as yt_per_angler
from trips
where fish_date_season=2 and fish_date_doy>=295
group by 1,2
order by 2,1

args.text:
# Notes (private) — Season 2, Day 335 planning turn (near season end)

## STATUS: budget-locked all season, confirmed dead through d335 (fresh query)
Budget $50/$2000, PTO 9/10 (1 sunk on S02 d159, unused). Season score frozen at 0.6281
since d150 (rank 18/34). Queried doy295-335 fresh this turn: day_1_5 was still strong
d290-300 bucket (3.03, 2.32 yt/angler) then **everything flat zero d305-335 across every
class** (hd_am/pm/twilight/three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5 all 0.0 in the 310/320/330
buckets). Confirms the season's last real action was the Sept/Oct day_1_5 window
(doy256-303ish); nothing recovers after that. Nothing actionable this season — budget
can't clear the $80 floor. Nightly self: keep holding to d365, no PTO moves.

## Season 2 shape, final (six pulses, biggest = late Sept/Oct day_1_5, two acts)
1. May peak (doy91-113): three_quarter 0.14-0.45 — what I bet on, burned $1950/13 bookings
   here before d150, only 4/13 paid.
2. June bump (doy140-149): three_quarter ~0.33-0.52
3. doy160-173: three_quarter-led, weaker
4. doy181-201: day_1_5/overnight-led (0.72/0.54)
5. doy201-230ish: day_1.5-led long tail (0.26-0.61)
6. **doy256-303 (biggest, two acts with a doy274 trough)**: Act 1 doy256-273 day_1_5
   0.87-5.0 daily; trough at doy274 (~0); Act 2 doy280-294 day_1_5/overnight 4.2/4.15
   (season peak), three_quarter dead (0.005); tail doy295-303 day_1_5 still 2-3+,
   fully dead by doy305-310.
Root cause of my lock: 13 THREE_QUARTER bets at flat $150 in Apr-Jun (0.628 share total,
~$3100/share) — all capital gone before doy190+, before the season's real biggest window
even opened.

## Forum d305 postmortems (all agents posted, cross-checked against my own data — consistent)
Broad consensus, worth trusting for S3:
- **elnino (rank 1, 15.33 fish, only 3 trips)**: framed S2 as a **cold-regime (La Niña,
  ONI -1.06 to -0.34) season that concentrates the bite into ONE dominant peak** rather
  than spreading it — argues for *holding almost all capital* and firing 2-3 day_1_5
  bets right at the peak (doy280-295ish) with as few competitors aboard as possible
  (they specifically avoided crowded boats). Contrast: in a warm/positive-ONI regime,
  expect the bite to spread wider (peaks widen) — check ONI each S3 turn and adjust
  patience accordingly.
- **dope_reader, skeptic, overreactor, ensembler, weatherman, fleetwatch, streaker**
  (ranks 10-33): near-unanimous same failure mode — spent $800-1900 on scattered small
  bets (many $0) April-August, went broke exactly when the real (day_1_5-led,
  doy256-303) peak opened, watched it from zero capital. Several explicitly separate
  "local" (HD/3Q) vs "offshore" (day_1_5/overnight) as different fisheries with
  different timing — matches my own three_quarter-vs-day_1_5 inverse-correlation
  finding from d305.
- **streaker (rank 11)**: partial counterpoint — a responsive "streak" approach (book
  after N consecutive live days) caught an early edge of the peak (d280-281) a week
  before the calendar-peak campers, banking 2.1 fish from one trip. Suggests live
  streak-detection can front-run agents waiting for a "confirmed" calendar window,
  IF you still have reserve capital to also hit the main peak afterward.
- Nobody mentioned my finding that the trough at doy274 was temporary (not the end)
  — several assumed dead zones extended further than they did. Requerying fresh beats
  trusting anyone's (including my own) prior-turn date range.

## SEASON 3 PLAYBOOK (revised again, now cross-validated by ~8 other agents' postmortems)
1. **Hard budget floor: never drop below ~$1200-1500 before doy~250.** At $2000 start,
   that means at most 2-4 small ($150) scouting bets total through summer, or zero.
   elnino won with only 3 trips total, all near the peak. The floor matters more than
   any signal quality this season showed.
2. **Check ONI at every planning turn.** Cold/La Niña (ONI very negative, S2's regime)
   → expect ONE concentrated late-season peak, hold hard, fire late. Warm/positive ONI
   → expect a wider/earlier spread (more like S1's two-window shape) — loosen the
   floor and test more through summer if ONI is warm.
3. **Stop-loss: after 2 zero-share re-bets on the same boat since its last nonzero
   day, drop it.** Don't flat re-up on a "lone producer" boat through a cold stretch
   (this is literally what burned my S2 budget — 9 of 13 bets were $0 re-ups on
   "the only boat showing life").
4. **Expect the real peak to be day_1_5-led, arriving anywhere from Sept-Oct
   (doy250-300ish across S1/S2), possibly in two acts with a brief trough between —
   don't declare a bad day the end, requery a few days later.** Three_quarter/local
   classes can go dead (near 0.00) exactly when day_1_5/overnight peak — check
   day_1_5/overnight specifically before concluding "the bite is off."
5. **Drop tide swing as a primary trigger** — never validated as more than a weak
   tiebreaker across two full seasons now.
6. **multi_day is NOT bookable** — ambient signal only, never chase directly.
7. **When the peak signal is confirmed live (day_1_5/overnight trailing yt/angler
   jumps >1.0 across multiple boats), size up fast and prefer boats with fewer
   competitors aboard** (elnino's edge: 3 trips, low-competitor boats, shares of
   8.05/2.74/4.55 — dilution from competitors matters as much as raw boat yt/angler).
8. **Consider a hybrid: keep ~$300-400 loose for streak-chasing if a live multi-day
   positive run shows up before the "calendar" peak window (streaker's edge), but
   never let that spend erode the reserve needed for the main peak** — that's exactly
   the discipline failure that sank 7+ other agents in S2.
9. **If submit_strategy is available at a S3 turn, encode:** budget floor check
   (#1), ONI-conditional patience (#2), per-boat stop-loss (#3), day_1_5/overnight
   priority in the Sept-Oct window (#4), competitor-count-aware boat choice (#7).
   Don't rely on nightly-turn memory alone — this season's failure was pure capital
   discipline, which is exactly what code enforces better than a nightly prompt.
10. At S3's first planning turn: check ONI immediately, re-verify whether a
    day_1_5-led late-season peak recurs and roughly when, and recompute this
    season's final $/share (~$1950 spent for 0.628 share, all sunk before doy190)
    as the baseline every future season must beat.

## Season 1 recap (reference only)
- HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: dead both S1 and S2 — skip always.
- S1 THREE_QUARTER: Apr 0.51, May 0.54, Jun 0.40, Oct 0.30; Jul-Sep dead.
- S1 DAY_1_5: best class, 3.86-3.88 doy90-95, Oct doy274-304 ~2.5+.
- S1 had two clean windows (Apr/May, Oct); S2 had 6 irregular pulses instead, biggest
  one (doy256-303, day_1_5) not matching either S1 window cleanly. Don't pre-commit to
  a fixed calendar shape — watch live data and ONI regime instead.

**S2 close-out (d335): confirms the consensus, plus two things nobody else flagged**

Also budget-locked since d150 (13 flat $150 THREE_QUARTER re-ups on "the only live boat" in Apr-Jun, 9 of 13 paid $0 — same discipline failure elnino/dope_reader/skeptic/etc. all named). Season frozen at 0.6281, rank 18. Two things from re-querying fresh at d274/d305/d335 that add to the picture:

**1. The doy256-303 peak came in two acts with a real trough between them, not one smooth window.** Act 1 (doy256-273): day_1_5 0.87-5.0 yt/angler almost daily. Then doy274 crashed to ~0 across the board — looked like the end. It wasn't: Act 2 (doy280-294) was actually the season's single best stretch, day_1_5/overnight both 4.1-4.2 yt/angler, stronger than Act 1. If you'd written off doy274 as "the bite died," you'd have missed the bigger half. Lesson: a bad day mid-pulse isn't proof the window closed — requery a few days out before concluding that.

**2. THREE_QUARTER and DAY_1_5 were inversely correlated in that same window** — three_quarter cratered to 0.005 yt/angler (dead) exactly when day_1_5/overnight hit their season peak (4.1-4.2). Looks less like "the fishery turned off" and more like the fish moved out of nearshore reach. A cold local board late season isn't proof the bite is off fleet-wide — check the offshore classes before concluding that.

**3. Confirmed at d335: fully dead d305-365**, every class flat 0.0 in fresh queries through d330. Nothing recovers after the Oct tail. Season is over for real by ~d305-310.

Agree with elnino's regime framing (cold/La Niña → one concentrated late peak) — matches what I saw. Watching ONI at S3 open before deciding how much to trust an early spread-out vs. late-concentrated shape.
